Shamballa Ho Chi Minh is a classic case of style over substance.
Jan 2026 • Family
Yes, the setting and ambience are undeniably beautiful. The space is serene, thoughtfully designed, and gives the impression of a refined dining experience. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Service levels are frankly lacklustre. Staff taking orders have a very poor command of English and were unable to recommend a single dish when asked. When I enquired about popular or signature items, the only response was to push a set menu—completely missing the point of the question. It felt lazy rather than helpful.

The food itself is wildly inconsistent. The tofu and cassava salad were decent, though hardly memorable. The momos were just passable—certainly not something you’d expect at these prices.

The worst offender was the outrageously priced truffle green curry. There was not even the faintest hint of truffle flavour. After complaining, they added “more truffle”, yet it still tasted nothing like truffle. I seriously doubt real truffle was used at all.

To make matters worse, this place is terrible at accommodating children. There are no child-friendly options on the menu, and when I asked if they could prepare something as simple as a basic noodle soup, the staff appeared completely panicked and unable to handle the request. For a restaurant positioning itself at this price point, that’s simply unacceptable.

In summary, this place charges international prices but delivers third-rate food and service. As an international and business traveller who has dined extensively around the world, I can confidently say this restaurant offers poor value, poor quality, and poor service.

Avoid.
